sub.description: subtracts a from b, a - b.

div.description: divides value a from b, a/b.

pwr.description: a**b, a^b, a with power b.

sqrt.description: value x when multiplied to itself gives a(input), thus; x*x = a

arithmetic_average.description: average; (a+b+c+...+n_term)/(no of terms), can be list

abs.description: absolute, if number n is < 0; then -(n), if 0; then 0; if > 0 then n.

min.description: minimum of the given values, can be list

max.description: maximum of the given values, can be list

random-int.description: generated a random integer between given inputs. 2 inputs(min, max);

random.description: generated a random number using computer entropy. generates a 13-16 digit number, HIGH RESOURCE!, NO inputs

round.description: rounds number to given decimal places, 2 inputs(input_number, decimal_places)

clamp.description: makes the value stay under desired values, 3 inputs(input_value, min_value, max_value)

normalize.description: returns normalized value restricted to 0 - 1. 5 inputs(input_value, min_value, max_value, new_min, new_max)

distance.description: gives distance between 2 points on a 1-D axis, value is absolute, 2 inputs(start-point, end-point)

sign.description: sign(x) returns -1 if x<0; returns 0 if x=0; returns 1 if x<1. 1 input(value)

abs_equal.description: absolute_equal gives Voolean True/False for 2 values if they are close enough by a certain threshold(value), 3 inputs(a_value, b_vlaue, threshold). NOTE-FLOATING POINT ERROR exists

apx_eql.description: approx_equal gives Boolean True/False for 2 values if they are 'close enough' or not by a threshold(relative), 3 inputs(a_value, b_value, threshold)

percent_equal.description: percent_equal gives Boolean True/False for 2 values if they are 'close enough' or not by a threshold in percent, 3 inputs(a_value, b_value, threshold)

in_range.description: in_range tell if value(x) is between low_value, and high_value, such that; low<x<high; if yes, then TRUE, else FALSE. 3 inputs(value, low_value, high_value).

wrap.description: value x to a specific range [min, max] by wrapping it back to the start if it exceeds the maximum, or back to the end if it falls below the minimum, 3 inputs(value, min, max)
